statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-96230 (GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4) is an ASP.NET Core remote code execution issue in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server: the Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated /_framework/debug endpoint used by dotnet watch. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server NuGet package as affected, from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/478, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix encodes the exception text in that package's debug page (TargetPickerUi) and in the debug-proxy page of the mono WebAssembly development server (dotnet/dotnet commit 2c81aaf1a5905b59c488aa176ef8ee1ade4a897f on release/10.0.1xx). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: no package contains a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server assembly or nupkg, a Blazor WebAssembly development server (DevServer), the BrowserDebugHost or BrowserDebugProxy debugging proxy, or any Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly assembly. The Blazor WebAssembly files they do hold are the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWebAssembly and Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WebAssembly build tasks of the .NET SDK (in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and as nupkg files in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts), with their debug symbol files in the symbols archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, the Microsoft.NET.WebAssembly.Threading reference package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, the Blazor WebAssembly project templates in the Microsoft.DotNet.Web.ProjectTemplates package (in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts and in the templates folder of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), and the WasmFeatures.props file of the Mono toolchain workload manifest (in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in a nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts), none of which contains the debug page. The same scan finds the ASP.NET Core Components server assembly (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll) in every build, so the search covers ASP.NET Core Components files. The affected package is not part of this owner.

CVE-2026-96230 (GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4) is an ASP.NET Core remote code execution issue in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server: the Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated /_framework/debug endpoint used by dotnet watch. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server NuGet package as affected, from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 for .NET 8, fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/478, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. We read all 220 packages of the ten builds published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0), every subpackage including the -dbg debug packages, for x86_64 and aarch64, recursing into the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold, and recorded every .NET assembly with its file version and every ELF, PE and Mach-O file. No package contains a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server assembly or nupkg, a Blazor WebAssembly development server (DevServer) assembly or nupkg, a BrowserDebugHost or BrowserDebugProxy assembly, or any Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly assembly or nupkg. A byte search of every .NET assembly in every package, including those inside nupkg files, finds no TargetPickerUi or UseWebAssemblyDebugging string; the affected package defines both for the /_framework/debug endpoint (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v8.0.31/src/Components/WebAssembly/Server/src/WebAssemblyNetDebugProxyAppBuilderExtensions.cs). The same scan finds the ASP.NET Core Components server assembly (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll) in every build, and the same byte search finds the TrySkipNextArray routine in that assembly in builds 8.0.23-r0 to 8.0.27-r0, so both searches reach ASP.NET Core Components files. The affected package is not part of this owner.

CVE-2026-96230 (GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4) is an ASP.NET Core remote code execution issue in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server: the Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated /_framework/debug endpoint used by dotnet watch. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server NuGet package as affected, from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 for .NET 9, fixed in 9.0.21 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qjpx-jqm5-h2c4, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/478, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: no package contains a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server assembly or nupkg, a Blazor WebAssembly development server (DevServer), the BrowserDebugHost or BrowserDebugProxy debugging proxy, a TargetPickerUi file, or any Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly assembly. The Blazor WebAssembly files they do hold are the build targets, tasks and tools of the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWebAssembly and Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WebAssembly SDKs (in the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and as nupkg files in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts), the Microsoft.NET.WebAssembly.Threading reference package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, the Blazor WebAssembly project templates in the Microsoft.DotNet.Web.ProjectTemplates package (in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts and in the templates folder of the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap), and the WasmFeatures.props file of the Mono toolchain workload manifest (in the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in a nupkg in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts), none of which contains the debug page. The same scan finds the ASP.NET Core Components server assembly (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll) in every build, so the search covers ASP.NET Core Components files. A string search of every .NET assembly in the 9.0.20-r0 x86_64 dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and dotnet9-runtime-artifacts packages, including those inside their nupkg files, finds no TargetPickerUi or UseWebAssemblyDebugging symbol; the only references to the /_framework/debug path are in the Blazor client script embedded in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Endpoints.dll, which requests that endpoint from a development server and does not serve the debug page. The affected package is not part of this owner.
